title: new04
live_proof: inspection in the 3.22.0 tree: fts3DestroyMethod() issues five fts3DbExec() calls in sequence, each evaluating p->zName at the call site, while an OOM inside one of them reaches fts3DisconnectMethod through sqlite3VdbeHalt -> sqlite3RollbackAll -> sqlite3ResetAllSchemasOfConnection -> sqlite3VtabUnlockList and sqlite3_free()s the Fts3Table. Fixed upstream in 3.27.0 by collapsing the five calls into one
object: the Fts3Table, freed by its own destructor running underneath it
lifetime_ender: a nested OOM triggers a schema reset that calls fts3DisconnectMethod while fts3DestroyMethod is still on the stack
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator, with OOM injected by a counting wrapper installed over memsys5 -- SQLITE_UNTESTABLE removes sqlite3_test_control, so the injection point is the allocator rather than SQLite's own test hook. The case reports its allocation count and the rc transition point so its sequence can be matched against the host oracle's

sublet.oracle: VM HALTED on a capability fault, cause 24 untagged dereference (temporal: revoked, or never a capability) pc=0x800239e4 -- taken outside the domain, so cooperative recovery has no frame to return through; all 28 halts in this arm are at the same kernel pc 0x800239e4

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT riscv64-purecap, memsys5 over the case's static arena (shared/run-cheribsd.py --mode nested). Revocation acts on a guest malloc free, and under memsys5 there is none: sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool inside one array the guest allocator sees as a single live object. So a tag fault here is NOT revocation reporting, and since 2026-10-30 it is not scored as a catch either: this arm is judged by the mechanism rule the virtual arms carry in tools/arms.json (catch_causes), under which an access the mechanism did not reject is MISSED however the program then crashes. A SIGPROT(34) si_code=2 at the function host ASan reported (fault_sites) is MISSED with the fault kept in its note; a fault anywhere else is not tied to the defect and stays NO-READING:unattributed. What the rule rests on is the configuration and not a silence: SQLITE_CONFIG_HEAP puts every SQLite allocation inside sqlite_heap[], sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool, and no free() ever reaches the guest allocator for a sweep to act on. The same harness with SYSALLOC=1 does emit allocator=system revoke=on-every-free on 31 of 33 cases (results/2026-10-29-cheribsd/non-nested), so the revoking path is live where it exists

virtual-platform.oracle: the same build without memsys5, where this case has no form at all: it reaches for sqlite_heap to engineer its OOM, and that array exists only when memsys5 is configured, so the builder reports it not applicable and the run scores NO-READING:out-of-denominator

cheribsd-platform.oracle: the same guest with memsys5 left OUT (shared/run-cheribsd.py --mode non-nested: the _sys binaries, SYSALLOC=1, run NOMEM5=1, which also forces a revoke at SQLite's allocator boundary). Every SQLite object is one of the guest malloc's, so its end IS a free the quarantine sees and revocation can act. SIGPROT(34) at the function host ASan reported (fault_sites), or the case returns and this arm did not see it. The cell is a reading of this arm only if the run records allocator=system and revoke=on-every-free for the case, which is repro_init()'s NOMEM5 branch saying it ran: a case whose run_case() does its own sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_HEAP) never calls repro_init() at all, so NOMEM5 does nothing to it and what ran was the nested configuration under the stock quarantine. 31 of the 33 record the marker; the two that do not are 07 and 22, the same two the Capstone builder reports not applicable, and both are NO-READING:out-of-denominator here for the same reason
cheribsd-platform.verdict_note: the run records neither allocator=system nor revoke=on-every-free for this case (results/2026-10-29-cheribsd/non-nested; 31 of the 33 cases do record both), because its run_case() installs memsys5 over sqlite_heap itself and so never reaches repro_init()'s NOMEM5 branch. What ran was the nested configuration under the stock quarantine, not this arm, so the silence it produced is not a reading of it. This matches the Capstone side, where the builder reports the case not applicable without memsys5
